value: seed germination does not respond to light: stored seeds germinated as well in light as in darkness
method: germination test, light (18 h photoperiod, 150 umol/m2/s PPF) versus dark (dishes wrapped in foil), constant 20 C, counted after 21 days
conditions: seeds stored at 4 C for 6 months; S. menziesii and S. canadensis tested alongside

source.title: Seed germination of burnet, Sanguisorba spp.

where: Results, Experiments 2, 3 and 4 (Experiment 2, light effects), Table 2; sentence requested verbatim from the fetch tool
quote: Seeds of all species germinated as well in light and dark (Table 2).
note: A null result for one response (germination). It does not show the plant lacks light sensing; the authors note Serigstad (1998) found light necessary for S. canadensis germination and suggest seed age may explain the difference.
